title: Choose the visual world for Overture
question: Dark techno is locked in. These are different takes on it. Keep the main one, pick an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Blacklight Door Stamp
options.lineage: the UV ink stamp on your wrist at a warehouse door, visible only under blacklight
options.thesis: The site is a dark room, and your cursor is the UV torch: rooms, gear and plans glow only where the light reaches.
materials: 1-bit dithered studio photos that turn full-colour under the light
options.viewport: Full-black screen. A huge OVERTURE stamp, its ink coming through bleed and grain. The cursor (or an automatic sweep on phones) lights up a real room photo underneath. BOOK A ROOM is stamped bottom-left, and the Nova/Hybrid/Vortex/Suite room picker is always visible.
options.risk: If the glow is overdone it slides into the stock 'neon on black' look; the stamp texture and the hand-inked edges have to carry it.

raised.raise: Strict two-tone discipline: every photo is dithered into stamp ink and ground until the UV light turns it into the real colour photo.
Length equals duration: each membership's hours are drawn as an exact proportional bar (6 / 12 / 16 / 20 h), not just written as a number.
One gesture drives everything: the same UV beam runs every reveal on every page, with no separate scroll effects.

options.label: Strobe & Fog Room
options.lineage: the club floor at 3am, fog and a single strobe
options.thesis: The page pulses at 128 BPM: each strobe flash freezes a frame of the studio.
options.viewport: Fog fills the screen and the logo hangs in it. Strobe hits reveal photos of the Vortex in time with the beat. The primary action is BOOK NOW.
options.risk: It's the familiar techno-site look, and the strobes need careful limits to stay safe for photosensitive visitors.

options.label: Signal Bench
options.lineage: CRT oscilloscope, phosphor trace on an etched graticule
options.thesis: Every room and plan is a signal you tune into on a phosphor graticule.
options.viewport: A live waveform from Web Audio drawn across the hero; knobs switch between rooms.
options.case: Producers recognise the scope; it holds on audience identification but loses some clarity for beginners.
options.risk: Can feel like a lab instrument rather than a club.

options.label: Torn Poster Wall
options.lineage: Toronto hoardings, layers of gig posters torn back
options.thesis: Tear down through layers of event posters to find rooms, plans and classes.
options.viewport: A wall of torn Overture posters; pulling a flap reveals the room beneath.
options.case: Rooted in local scene culture, but grey paper reads less dark-techno than the brief asks.
options.risk: Drifts toward punk/indie rather than techno.

options.label: One-bit Desktop
options.viewport: Overlapping windows, each one a room.
options.case: Nostalgic computing, not a club; DJs don't see themselves in it.
options.kept: Strict two-tone dithered photography until the UV light reveals the colour.

options.label: Dance Score
options.case: White paper and choreography notation, so it misses the techno brief.
options.kept: Length equals exact duration, used for the membership hour bars.

options.label: Miura Fold
options.thesis: One pull unfolds a whole sheet.
options.viewport: A packet unfolding into a sail.
options.case: Light, precise and aerospace in feel, with no link to the club world.
options.kept: One control runs the whole system: the UV beam drives every reveal.

canonCard.label: Standard dark club site
canonCard.thesis: The typical nightlife/studio site, done really well.
canonCard.viewport: Full-screen room video, big condensed headline, BOOK NOW button.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every other studio and club site in the city.
